9.0.0.en: 1 Be not jealous over the wife of thy bosom, and teach her not an evil lesson against thyself. 2 Give not thy soul unto a woman, lest she rule over thy strength.

9.0.1.en: Be not jealous of the wife in thy bosom, so that thou givest her an evil example that harms thee [1].

9.0.2.en: Ben Sira begins by affirming his esteem for marriage. At the same time he reveals a grave plague that corrupts the purity of the family, namely the creeping in of suspicion toward one of the members of the family, especially the wife. The wife may act with some simplicity, and it is fitting for the husband to deal with her wisely, lest by his extreme jealousy he spoil her simplicity, and she think that his suspicion of her is the fruit of the impurity of his own heart. Nor is it fitting for the husband to be jealous of his wife for the gifts, abilities, and potentials she enjoys, lest he become an evil example in her eyes.

9.0.3.en: Mutual trust between the spouses: Solomon the Wise says: "Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies. The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil. She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life" (Prov 31:10-12). Origen says that the wife is like the Garden of Eden, in which are the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil [1].

9.1.0.en: Do not give thy soul unto a woman, lest she tread upon thy strength [2].

9.1.1.en: Suspicion of the wife is often a kind of extremism, causing tension in the whole family, yet on the other hand a person's giving up his soul to the other party, that is, to the wife or the husband, is often at the expense of the family's spiritual building up. He who places himself under the authority of a woman (he probably means his wife) will have her despise his dignity (Prov 31:3). The partnership between them does not mean that one dominates the other, and humility does not mean leaving matters without management.

9.2.0.en: 3 Meet not with an harlot, lest thou fall into her snares. 4 Use not much the company of a woman that is a singer, lest thou be taken with her attempts. 5 Gaze not on a maid, lest thou stumble by her beauty. 6 Give not thy soul unto harlots, lest thou lose thine inheritance.

9.2.1.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that the enemy uses his wiles and powers to destroy man's inner purity, and therefore it is fitting for the believer to set out like a bird soaring in the heavenly places, so that he cannot be captured by a satanic snare.

9.2.2.en: For the sake of purity of heart, Ben Sira asks his disciples to avoid clinging to a strange woman, who may catch him in her net (Prov 7:23), and to avoid gazing at a virgin with lustful thoughts, lest he stumble and be exposed to punishment.

9.2.3.en: Do not meet an adulterous woman, lest thou fall into her snares [3].

9.2.4.en: What is meant here is a lewd woman frequented by those of wealth and authority. Ben Sira often warned his disciples against forming relationships with women through indulgence and carelessness (25:13-26; 18; 42:9-14). He warns of the moral danger of associating with licentious women. It is written in the book of Proverbs: "Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings" (Prov 31:3). "For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit" (Prov 23:27). "For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life. Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?" (Prov 6:26-27).

9.3.0.en: Do not tarry long with a dancer, lest thou be caught by her wiles [4].

9.3.1.en: He asks them that none of them prolong his stay with a licentious dancer [4].

9.4.0.en: Do not gaze on a virgin, lest thou stumble and cause her harm [5].

9.4.1.en: He does not ask his disciples to close their eyes, but not to gaze at her. As the Lord Christ says: "Whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart" (Mt 5:28). Ben Sira fears falling into sin with a virgin, for the penalty for that in the Old Testament was most severe (Deut 22:28-29). Righteous Job says: "I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?" (Job 31:1).

9.5.0.en: Do not give thy soul unto harlots, lest thou lose thine inheritance [6].

9.5.1.en: He calls them not to give their souls to lewd women, for their souls are holy brides in the hand of the holy heavenly Bridegroom. Samson the mighty gave himself to Delilah, and she was able to humble him; she gave the enemies the opportunity to put out his eyes, and he worked in the mill like an ox (Judg 16:4-21). St. Jacob of Serugh says:

9.5.2.en: [Alas for Samson the Nazirite, who became a mockery, a laughingstock and a disgrace to the generations to come.

9.5.3.en: The mighty in valor who overcame the lion in battle fell into the hands of a woman, O the great shame!

9.5.4.en: Like a serpent she bit the Nazirite, and his hair fell from him, and he became weak, wretched, helpless, and reeling.

9.5.5.en: No sooner had the Philistines snared the lion than they gathered to mock the man who had multiplied their slain.

9.5.6.en: In their rage they plucked out his eyes, and humbled his splendor, and put out his shining lamp and his sight.

9.5.7.en: They laid upon him a dreadful and conspicuous stain, and the great one was brought down to great disgrace.

9.5.8.en: They took him and bound him, and he ground in the prison house, and it was an occasion of great celebration for the Philistines [2].]

9.6.s.en: 3. Purity on the public road and at banquets

9.6.0.en: 7 Look not round about thee in the streets of the city, neither wander thou in the solitary places thereof. 8 Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty. 9 For many have been led astray by the beauty of a woman, and by it love is kindled as a fire. 10 Every woman that is an harlot shall be trodden under foot as dung in the way. 11 Many have been bewitched by the beauty of a strange woman, and their lot was disgrace, for converse with her is kindled as a fire. 12 Sit not at all with another man's wife, nor lean with her on the elbow. 13 And be not a companion with her in wine, lest thy soul incline unto her, and so thou slide with thine heart into destruction.

9.6.1.en: Do not let thine eyes roam in the streets of the city, nor wander in its desolate corners [7].

9.6.2.en: Ben Sira did not forbid his disciples to walk in the streets of the city, but calls them to sanctify their sight like Joseph the pure young man, whose garment Potiphar's wife seized, but he realized that the eyes of the Lord were looking upon him (Gen 39:13). It was said of him: "a goodly person, and well favoured" (Gen 39:6), and by leaving the garment in the hands of his mistress he revealed his purity and the beauty of his soul and the sweetness of his heart, and as Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles, says: [Joseph was more beautiful within than without, radiant with the light of his heart more than with the beauty of his body, for the eyes of this woman could not penetrate and enjoy his beauty [3].] And St. John Chrysostom says: [Joseph was stripped and became more radiant than others, as though he had returned to the state of Adam naked in Paradise and not ashamed, because of his purity [4].] And St. Clement of Alexandria calls us to control and sanctify the senses, for it is not fitting for the believer to let his eyes roam here and there like one lost in the streets, nor for the feet to wander in desolate corners. [What is the desolate corner? "The desolate place is the place where there is no pure person, even if there is a noisy crowd in it [5].] It is fitting for us to sanctify the eye by Christ the light of the world (Jn 8:12), and the feet by Christ the Way (Jn 14:6).

9.6.3.en: Turn thy gaze away from a beautiful woman, and do not gaze at a strange beauty.

9.7.0.en: For the beauty of a woman has led many astray, and by it lust is kindled like fire [8].

9.7.1.en: He asks not to gaze at a beautiful woman, because the sin is not in her beauty, but in gazing with an evil will.

9.7.2.en: v And if you want to know the reason, look within yourself, for the beauty of a woman has led many men astray, and by it lust is kindled like fire. The friendship that begins in fire, which is called passion, cannot be quenched in its sin, but returns to the fire [6].

9.7.3.en: St. Clement of Alexandria v Where do the Holy Scriptures speak of sin and its causes? They accuse those who lived before the Flood of practicing impure relations. Hear how it shows the cause: "The sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives (of them)" (Gen 6:2).

9.7.4.en: v Was beauty the cause of the sin? That cannot be! In truth, beauty is the work of the wisdom of God, and the work of God will not be the cause of evil. Then was their sin that they looked at them? No, seeing is a natural act. What then? They looked at them with an evil intention, which is truly the fruit of an evil will. For this reason Wisdom gives us this counsel: "Do not gaze at a beautiful (strange) woman." It did not say: "Do not look," not because this happens spontaneously. Rather it says: "Do not gaze," meaning the deliberate scrutiny, the disturbing gazing and the long-range thinking that comes from a corrupt soul which is the prey of lust.

9.7.5.en: And what is the loss, if a person looks and is able to withdraw from it? Following this comes "the love that is kindled like fire." Indeed, after fire catches the stubble and the straw at once and without need of time, it catches the wood and kindles a blazing fire. So also the fire of lust that is in us, after it becomes a flame in a beautiful and lofty image through the work of the eyes, at once burns the souls of those who gaze [7].

9.7.6.en: v One of the (wise men) gives this counsel: "Do not gaze at a strange beauty, nor meet with a woman who is addicted to adultery" (see Sir 9:3, 8). For honey drops from the lips of the harlot, who for a time seems smooth to your throat, and afterward you find her more bitter than gall, and sharper than a two-edged sword (Prov 5:3-4). For the harlot does not know how to love, but only how to hunt. In her kiss there is poison, and her mouth is a deadly narcotic. If this does not appear at once, she must be avoided all the more for this reason, because she conceals destruction, and covers over that death, and does not allow it to appear at the beginning [8].

9.8.0.en: v He did not say only: "He who desires," for a person can desire even if he is sitting alone on the mountains. Rather Jesus said: "He who looks with lust," meaning that a person thinks of another merely out of the desire for lust, he who is under no compulsion allows the wild beast to enter by force into his thoughts while they are calm. This intrusion does not come from nature, but from laxity toward the soul. The Old Testament corrects this from the beginning, saying: "Do not gaze at the beauty of another" (see Sir 9:8) [9].

9.9.0.en: St. John Chrysostom v It is right, before everything, to flee from looking at women, for sin is not in touching only but in seeing also, and we must train ourselves to avoid it. "Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee" (Prov 4:25). It is possible for one who looks at women to remain steadfast, but he needs to guard against falling. It is possible for one who looks to fall, but it is impossible for one who does not look to fall into sexual lust. It is not enough for the chaste to be pure, but he must strive to pass beyond the sphere of blame and be free of all earthly preoccupations for the sake of fulfilling purity. Not only that we may be believers but that we may be worthy of the trust. For this reason St. Paul the Apostle says concerning taking care: "Avoiding this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us: Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men" (2 Cor 8:20-21). Holy Scripture says: "Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty" (see Sir 9:8). And if you want to know the reason for this saying of Scripture, it adds: "For many have been led astray by the beauty of a woman, and by it love is kindled as a fire" (see Sir 9:8). The feeling that arises from fire, which we call love, leads to a fire that is not quenched, and that is the end of sin [10].

9.9.1.en: St. Clement of Alexandria: Do not dine with a woman who is married to another, and do not join her in parties with wine, lest thy soul incline unto her, and thou go down with thy spirit into destruction [9].

9.9.2.en: He called them not to take pleasure in wine, especially with a woman married to another. The mother of Solomon counseled her son: "It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for the great strong drink" (Prov 31:4).

9.9.3.en: v It is a good commandment that Wisdom offers: "Sit not at all with another man's wife, nor lie back on a couch with her," that is, do not dine or eat much with her. Then he added: "Do not take pleasure in wine with her, lest thy heart incline unto her, and thou go down with thy desire into destruction" (see Sir 9:9).

9.10.0.en: Drinking without restraint is dangerous, because it can easily bring thee down into licentiousness [11].

9.11.0.en: 14 Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him. 15 A new friend is as new wine; when it is old, thou shalt drink it with pleasure.

9.11.1.en: After he commanded reserve on the public road and at banquets and parties, he urged believers to practical counsels, among them to prize the old friend and not to abandon him [10].

9.11.2.en: Do not forsake an old friend, for the new is not equal to him.

9.11.3.en: A new friend is like new wine; when it is old, thou shalt drink it with pleasure [10].

9.11.4.en: Forming a friendship with someone and then abandoning him reveals that he built the friendship on temporal benefit. Friendship is not used for temporary profit, but is the pledge of the heavenly love which not even death destroys, but which grows without ceasing, and which we live in eternity. Loyalty to the old friend is regarded as a great virtue. St. Augustine sees the old friend as prizing the Old Testament, which announced the New Testament by prophecies and types: [Were it not for the Old Testament I would not have believed in the New Testament.] And his disciple Fulgentius came to declare the New Testament's esteem for the role of the Old Testament.

9.11.5.en: v It is fitting that the Old Testament be kept with honor in such a way that it is neglected in no way. This, as it seems to me, is what Ben Sira meant, when he commands under the figure of the old and the new friend, saying: "Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him." The divine Scripture spoke by the mouth of Jeremiah, looking to the difference in the mysteries of the two covenants: "Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah" (Jer 31:31) [12].

9.11.6.en: Fulgentius: This friendship with the eternal God is manifested through the relationship of Moses the prophet with Him, for it is said: "And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend" (Ex 33:11). St. Gregory, bishop of Nyssa, says: [O Caesarius, man of God, I have written you this briefly concerning what pertains to the perfection of the virtuous life, and I have sketched something like a pattern of the life of the great Moses, so that each of us may imitate the image of the beauty that appears to us in it by imitating the manner of life of Moses. And there is no evidence that Moses attained perfection more than the divine voice which said to him: "Thou hast found grace in my sight, and I know thee by name" (Ex 33:12, 17), and also that he was called the friend of the Lord: "And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend" (Ex 33:11) [13].]

9.11.7.en: And in the New Testament St. John the Baptist said of himself that he was the friend of the bridegroom (Jn 3:29), who rejoiced as he saw many gathering around the Lord Christ, as the bride sanctified by the Lord. The role of the friend of the bridegroom among the Jews was important and indispensable, and he was exempted from some religious obligations to devote himself to helping the newly married, especially in the first seven days of the marriage. His work before the marriage was to care for the betrothed and guard her and give testimony to the bridegroom about her; and he served as the link between them, carrying the messages of each to the other, since the betrothed was not allowed to leave the house. After the marriage he strengthened the personality of the bride; he slept in a flat next to the dwelling of the couple to prevent any harm from befalling the bride. And he did not allow either party to deceive the other, and it was his duty to examine the purity of the bride, and when he was assured of that he exulted and rejoiced. Perhaps this is what St. John meant by his saying: "This my joy therefore is fulfilled" (Jn 3:29). He presents the gifts that come to the couple, and finally takes part in the joyful celebration of the marriage for seven days. After this celebration the friend of the bridegroom becomes like the defender of the bride (2 Cor 11:2), and he settles any problems that arise between them.

9.11.8.en: v It is as though John the Baptist said: I would have suffered much had this not come to pass. If the bride had not come forward to her bridegroom, I would then have been pained and distressed by it, but I am not grieved now that my hopes are fulfilled, and everything we wished has been accomplished, and the bride has known her bridegroom, and you have testified to it, and since I have seen this request fulfilled, I am glad and rejoice (as a friend of the bridegroom).

9.12.s.en: 5. Purity in our view of the successful wicked

9.12.0.en: 16 Envy not the glory of a sinner: for thou knowest not what shall be his end. 17 Be not pleased with the pleasure of the hypocrites. Remember that they shall not be justified unto Hades.

9.12.1.en: Do not envy the honor given to a sinner, for thou knowest not what his end shall be [11].

9.12.2.en: The Psalmist asked: "Why does the way of the wicked prosper?", and the answer came: "Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity. For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb. Trust in the LORD, and do good; dwell in the land, and feed on faithfulness" (Ps 37:1-3).

9.12.3.en: Do not rejoice in what pleases the wicked, and remember that even in the abode of the dead they are not justified [12].

9.12.4.en: v "Fret not thyself because of evildoers, for they shall soon wither like the grass." Tell me, what is the fate of him who plunders and robs after his departure? Was not all that he had a dream and an illusion?!... But such is not the state of the saints; you cannot utter the same words about their state, and do not say that what belongs to them is a dream and a legend [14].

9.13.s.en: 6. Dealing carefully with the wicked mighty

9.13.0.en: 18 Keep far from him that hath power to kill, and the fear of death will not come into thy mind. 19 And if thou come near him, do not offend, lest he take away thy life. 20 Know that thou goest in the midst of snares, and walkest upon the bulwarks of the cities.

9.13.1.en: He encourages his disciples to associate with the wise, the pious, those who fear the Lord (Prov 13:20).

9.13.2.en: Keep far from him that hath power to kill, so that thou be not troubled with the fear of death.

9.13.3.en: And if thou come near him, do not provoke him, lest he put an end to thy life.

9.13.4.en: Know that thou steppest among snares, and walkest around the archery towers of the city [13].

9.13.5.en: It is well that his disciples keep away from those who have the power to kill, and so avoid the danger of death [13].

9.13.6.en: v If we use every means and spare no effort to avoid the death of the body, how much more must we strive to avoid the death of the spirit?! For there is no obstacle before a man who desires salvation, except the neglect and slackness of the soul [15].

9.13.7.en: St. Anthony the Great v Know that thou walkest in the midst of snares, and that thou goest to an archery tower beside the city [13]. Everything is full of snares; Satan fills everything with nets. But when the Word of God comes to you... you will say: "Our souls are escaped like a sparrow from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we are escaped. We are blessed in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth" (see Ps 124:7)...

9.13.8.en: Jesus prepares the way for you. He came down to earth and subjected Himself to the nets of the world. When He saw the great flock of humanity imprisoned in the nets, and saw that He alone was able to tear them, He came to the nets, and took a human body and subjected it to the nets of the mighty enemy, and tore them to pieces for your sake [16].

9.13.9.en: Origen v "Know thyself," that is, examine yourself from every corner. Keep the eyes of your soul as sleepless guards, for you are walking in the midst of snares (see Sir 9:13). The enemy has set hidden nets in every place. Look at yourself in all directions, and so you will be saved like the swallow from the traps and the sparrow from the snares (Prov 6:5). But the gazelle cannot fall into a snare because of the strength of its sight [17].

9.13.10.en: St. Basil the Great v In truth we need more defense, seeing that there are ambushes on every side. This is as Solomon says in counsel: "Know that thou goest in the midst of snares, and walkest upon the walls of the cities." How many good things this saying means!... Let each of us write it in his mind, and let us carry it always in our memory, so that we do not fall easily into sin... Even boys hide snares in the ground; so Satan covers our sins with the pleasures of life... There are snares in the house, snares at the table, and snares in social relations [18].

9.13.11.en: v As the birds, so long as they cling to the upper layers of the air, cannot be easily caught, so you, as long as you look to the things above, cannot be captured, whether in a snare or by any other means.

9.14.0.en: The devil is a fowler of birds. Soar on high above his arrows [19].

9.15.s.en: 7. Purity in social gatherings and banquets

9.15.0.en: 21 Test men as much as thou canst, and consult with the wise among them. 22 Let just men be thy companions at table, and let thy glorying be in the fear of the Lord. 23 Make thy company with the prudent, and let all thy talk be in the law of the Most High.

9.15.1.en: At family and church banquets it is fitting for us to choose to sit with righteous people whom we may imitate and whose blessing we may seek, and what occupies us is the law of God.

9.15.2.en: Assess thy relatives as much as thou canst, and consult with the wise [14].

9.15.3.en: Let thy talk be with the wise, and all thy words in the law of the Most High [15].

9.15.4.en: The firm and strong friendship is that which is based on the Lord's dwelling between the two friends, and their guidance according to the divine commandment. Holy friendship is concerned with speaking of the great things of God and exchanging spiritual experiences.

9.15.5.en: v Christ says: "Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures" (Mt 22:29). And Paul also said: "That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope" (Rom 15:4). And also: "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable" (2 Tim 3:16). "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly" (Col 3:16). And the prophet says: "In his law doth he meditate day and night" (Ps 1:2). And in another place: "Let all thy talk be in the law of the Most High" (Sir 9:15)... Believe me, nothing strong, nothing useful comes forth from us [20].

9.15.6.en: v Let us adorn all the rest of your time also with practice in the laws of God. "Let... all thy talk be in the law of the Most High" (see Sir 9:15). As we adorn ourselves thus, let us come to our King, and fall on our knees, not only with the body, but with the mind also. Let us consider who this is to whom we draw near, and on whose account, and what we are accomplishing. We draw near to God, upon whom the seraphim gaze, covering their faces, unable to bear His splendor, He before whose sight the earth trembles [21].

9.15.7.en: St. John Chrysostom Let the righteous be thy companions at table, and let thy glorying be in the fear of the Lord [16].

9.16.0.en: Besides our concern to choose wise men who love the law of God in social gatherings, family banquets and church occasions, it is also fitting that the fear of the Lord prevail in them, and that they bear witness to a life of righteousness in the Lord. St. Basil was concerned with a special order and arrangement for the table, as he was concerned with table manners, and laid down the following principles [22]:

9.17.0.en: a. He requires all to partake of food with thanksgiving to God [23].

9.18.0.en: b. During the meal a reading from the Holy Bible is read [it must be listened to with greater pleasure than the pleasure we have as we eat and drink, so that our minds may appear undistracted by bodily pleasure, but rather rejoice in the words of the Lord, like him who found them "sweeter than honey and the honeycomb" [24].]

9.18.1.en: c. To sit, as far as possible, in the last place at the table in a spirit of humility.

9.18.2.en: d. To keep quiet in movements and voice.

9.18.3.en: e. The believer does not allow himself to fill his stomach and be satisfied.

9.18.4.en: f. He does not enter into idle discussions, even in choosing the last place, and if he sees a man seeking the place, he leaves it to him. And if he senses quarrels over the last place, he is bound to obey the one responsible for preparing the table. Obedience to him is better than choosing the last place through useless disputes.

9.19.s.en: 8. A life of purity and dealing with the various classes of the people

9.19.0.en: 24 The work is commended for the hand of the artificers, and the ruler of the people is wise for his speech. 25 A man of ready tongue is feared in his city, and he that babbleth in his talk is hated.

9.19.1.en: The purity of the believer is evident even in his esteem for every person, whatever his class, education, or work, for we need the simple worker and the wise ruler. Without workers and craftsmen the city does not stand. What concerns us is that all be faithful in the little that is in their hands. While avoiding the talkative man, and also the rash in his speech [18].

9.19.2.en: The work of the hands of the craftsmen is commended, and the leader of the people is wise for his speech [17].

9.19.3.en: All humanity will stand on the great day of the Lord for judgment, and what distinguishes them is the measure of their faithfulness in the little that was in their hands in the world, that they may be entrusted with the much that is given in eternity to the faithful.

9.19.4.en: The talkative man is feared in his city, and he who is rash in his speech is hated [18].

9.19.5.en: v Beware of coarseness in speech, for humility and chastity are among the marks of the wise...

9.20.0.en: The thought that loves God is a light that shines for the soul, as the sun shines for the body [25].

9.20.2.en: Grant us the spirit of purity, O Holy One!

9.20.3.en: v When humanity joins the choir of the heavenly ones, they sing, saying: Holy, holy, holy! May all sanctify You in their lives wherever they may be!

9.20.4.en: v Remember, O Lord, every family, and dwell in it!

9.20.5.en: In purity the husband is not jealous over his wife or of her. He does not envy her gifts and abilities.

9.20.6.en: Nor does suspicion enter between the spouses, so that the whole family is made worthy of the simplicity of the heavenly ones and their love and mutual esteem among them!

9.20.7.en: v Be, O my God, the leader of the family, so that neither of them gives himself up to the other, but You lead all.

9.20.8.en: And neither makes light of the other, for all are Your children, longing to be Your icon!

9.20.9.en: v Grant us the spirit of wisdom filled with love and purity in seriousness!

9.20.10.en: So that no one clings to a harlot in indulgence and carelessness, and no one wastes his time in licentiousness and slackness.

9.20.11.en: Let not the eyes of a young man gaze at a virgin, lest he stumble! Nor let him give himself up to a harlot who destroys his inheritance.

9.20.12.en: v Let our eyes gaze upon You and be filled with radiance. Let the inner vision be sanctified and be lifted up to glories.

9.20.13.en: We do not loiter in the streets of the city, for the gates of the heavenly Jerusalem are open to us, and the heavenly ones are occupied with us!

9.20.14.en: v Open our inner sight, that we may see, in the spirit of purity, the table which You prepare for us!

9.20.15.en: It is no man who gives us enjoyment, but You are the desire of our hearts!

9.20.16.en: What parties offer us entertainment? Rather Your banquet fills our depths with joy and delight!

9.20.17.en: v What friend loved us before our creation as You did? And who died on the cross to raise us to the eternal glories?

9.20.18.en: You are the old Friend who satisfies all our depths. You give us love and purity, so that our heart is enlarged for all mankind.

9.20.19.en: v You used to converse with Moses the prophet as a man speaks to his friend (Ex 33:11).

9.20.20.en: Your friendship has given us a new creation; You removed evil from us and gave us Your divine righteousness!

9.20.21.en: Our meeting with You raises up from us wise and prudent men!

9.20.22.en: v Take hold of my hand, and turn my life into a joyful journey toward heaven!

9.20.23.en: Lift me from glory to glory until I meet You.

9.20.24.en: Lift me from the dust of the world, and rescue me from the devil's snares, hidden and manifest.

9.20.25.en: v Grant me to meet Your wise children, that I may learn purity from them, and enjoy a constructive friendship.

9.20.26.en: It is sweet for us to speak together about You and about Your law.

9.20.27.en: We hold fast to Your divine promises, and grow in Your fear, and find Your love sweet!

9.20.28.en: I do not despise a poor man nor a simple worker, for I see Your image shining in their hearts, and Your joy manifest on their faces.

9.20.29.en: v Let me be silent, that I may hear the voice of my heart, and listen to Your words.

9.20.30.en: I do not find chatter with a man sweet, nor do I walk in a spirit of rashness.

9.20.31.en: By Your Holy Spirit my being is shaped day by day, that Your icon may shine forth in me, and I be made worthy of the heavenly wedding feast!
